gap: Street-level lived-in density in B. Within about 40 m of the camera the frame must show at least 5 distinct pieces of weathered street clutter (signage, poles and overhead wires, bins, stalls or awnings, parked vehicles) and at least 3 pedestrians. Road and building surfaces must show visible grime or wear (stains, patching, cracks, decals). No bare, uniform asphalt or grass area may cover more than about 25% of the frame.

better_than_baseline=false. Baseline: I compared every one of the 16 --photos and 7 --gameplay-photos views and route 06 against progress/img/baseline/ (same cameras; no fixed view moved). Sheets: /private/tmp/opus55/critic/materials-B1/evidence/sheet_baseline-left_ours-right_*.jpg.

Clear wins, all aerial or ground-plane:
- Aerial roofs: the blank beige or dark box roofs in photos 06, 07, 09 and 16 now have parapets, rooftop plant and window rows. Paved lots, the hawker plaza (gameplay 04), the helipad apron (09) and the workshop floor (14) now read as weathered concrete slabs instead of flat brown or navy.
- Background box buildings gained windows and AC units: photo 02 left block, photo 11.
- Asphalt is no longer near-black. Mean road luminance rose 29->50 (photo 01), 39->69 (photo 02), 53->86 (gameplay 03) and 90->113 (route 06), with cracks, a manhole and oil stains.

Mixed or worse at street level, which is the part a player sees most:
- photo 08_street_arcade regressed. The left arcade facade luminance fell 41.4->32.6 (-21%) and saturation 20.5->17.2. The columns became streaky near-black, the five-foot way is murkier, the new AC condenser is a crude white box with a black disc, and the road has a streaky wet-looking sheen although everything else is dry.
- Shophouse pastels are muted. Facade luminance fell 66.6->59.5 (photo 01), 120.6->103.9 (gameplay 01) and 108->100 (gameplay 03), and saturation dropped slightly.
- New artefacts:
  - hard-outlined rectangular patch quads on the carriageway (gameplay 03 foreground, route 06, gameplay 01);
  - double-yellow and white markings over-distressed, with camouflage-like black splotches (gameplay 07 stop line, route frame at 70 s);
  - the convenience-store interior floor (photo 12) now clearly shows cracked road asphalt with a patch outline.
- Unchanged: void deck about 70% dark (photo 04), hawker interior, safe room.

Performance, contaminated (shared GPU, editor binary, back-to-back): dressing on gave route p50/p95/p99 of 11.84/17.11/18.79 ms; --clean-surfaces gave 11.84/17.28/19.07 ms. So no measurable cost, and draws went from 1072 to 1143 multimesh. No hitch above 1 s: the largest non-capture stall was 355 ms at start-up.

Verdict: the aerial and ground-plane views are clearly better; street level is a mix of gains and new regressions. Not clearly better overall.. Singapore: It still reads as Singapore. At street level: shophouse rows with five-foot ways and green louvred shutters; Kopitiam, Rice Shop, Stationery, Phone Repair and Sari Textiles signage; the Tembusu Food Centre hawker pavilion; HDB slabs; double-yellow kerb lines; left-hand traffic. In the skyline: Marina Bay Sands, the Supertrees and the Flyer.

But this materials pass moves away from CONCEPT-01/02 and SG-01 (Joo Chiat), which show crisp, well-kept pastel conservation shophouses with Peranakan tiles, crisp intact LTA-style markings, drain grates and bollards. Ours makes the shophouses darker and greyer with rain streaks and grime (the arcade in photo 08 is the worst). It chips the double-yellow and white markings into fragments and black splotches, and adds generic patch rectangles. The result reads as a run-down generic city.

Tropical mould streaks are appropriate on HDB and concrete blocks; they are not appropriate on conservation shophouses or road paint. The Peranakan tile panels, five-foot-way floor tiles, drain grates and bollards from the concept are still absent.

Aerially (CONCEPT-03), the new uniform cream infill blocks and the large bare concrete lots do not read as Singapore's terracotta-roof and tree-canopy fabric.

- No reference image was blocked and no render was refused. All of my runs acquired the lease, with at most about 1-2 minutes of queueing.. Judge: The same image won every pair. In pairs 1, 2 and 3 it was A, in pair 4 it was B; in each case it was the clean frame with no HUD. Pair 2 was the closest: the winning frame there is visibly older and lower-resolution, with harsh flat light, and won only on believability, prop storytelling and character presence. The HUD frames (which all look like the same Singapore-themed project) lose for the same reasons each time. Streets and lots are sparse and empty. Landmarks and skylines are blockout-grade: extruded towers with repeated window decals, wireframe-like supertrees, rows of identical boxes, an untextured black box. Surfaces lack weathering and clutter, and characters are low-fidelity and stiff. In pair 3 the car is on the median, ploughing through shrubs. Their real strength is soft, warm late-day lighting, which sometimes beats the older winning frame. The most important fix is filling the near and mid-ground with weathered, specific set dressing and life, and replacing the blockout landmarks and towers. Caveat for the experiment: the pairs are not truly blind. Three of the winning frames carry a visible 'Grand Theft Auto V' logo and every losing frame carries the same gameplay HUD, so the source is obvious. The HUD also hurts the losing frames on composition. For a fairer test, crop or remove watermarks and HUDs before judging. I based my verdicts on visual quality only.
